name: Monitoring And Alerting Checklist
description: This module is a short pre-completion checklist of specific items to verify before marking any monitoring and alerting task, implementation, or piece of work complete.
content:
This module is a short pre-completion checklist of specific items to verify before marking any monitoring and alerting task, implementation, or piece of work complete.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Document any non-obvious monitoring and alerting decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
2. When monitoring and alerting decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
3. Prefer the simplest monitoring and alerting approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
4. Keep monitoring and alerting changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
5. Surface known limitations of a chosen monitoring and alerting approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
6. Measure before optimizing any monitoring and alerting bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
7. Check that monitoring and alerting terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
8. Validate monitoring and alerting outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
9. When monitoring and alerting guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
10. Keep monitoring and alerting outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
11. When multiple monitoring and alerting strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not apply generic monitoring and alerting advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not skip documenting monitoring and alerting assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Avoid mixing unrelated monitoring and alerting concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not silently drop monitoring and alerting edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of monitoring and alerting correctness.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for monitoring and alerting, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
